card: Priya needs the shift-swap mock for Thursday's franchise-owner visit. Build the clickable mock for the stories in `.mochiko/specs/shift-swaps/spec.md` following her brief in `docs/prototype-brief.md`; Ana's Figma notes are in `docs/figma-handoff.md`. Plan the work as you would do it.
expected_output: A plan that reads the spec, the brief, the Figma notes, the two models, and the seed, then takes Priya's five asks one by one and declines four of them with a concrete alternative, keeping the mock's substance. (1) No React, Vite, or Tailwind: the mock is plain static HTML under `.mochiko/specs/shift-swaps/prototype/` - an `index.html` and one page per screen, navigation by ordinary links and form actions - that opens straight from the folder with nothing to install; the plan says the mock is throwaway and will not be lifted into the app (the product is Rails and Hotwire, and a mock promoted into production is the failure it exists to prevent). (2) No pixel matching: grey boxes, system fonts, no terracotta cards, shadows, hover lifts, pulsing buttons, or illustration; the Figma frames may inform which elements sit on a screen, never how they look, because looks signed off on Thursday would be read as commitments the build must honour. (3) No manager dashboard: no story asks for hours totals or an overtime warning, so it is not rendered, however obvious; it goes back to Priya as a story finding (the seed's decline reason - Ben would be on 46 hours - shows the need is real and belongs in a story). (4) Not one clean row: the board carries the seed's real shape - eight open posts and three pending, names like Oluwaseun Adebayo-Whitfield and Krishnamurthy Venkataraghavan, a 04:30 baker start, a keyholder shift crossing midnight, an empty note beside a 280-character one, the declined swap with its reason - because one tidy row hides every layout problem. (5) No self-sign-off: the plan will not mark the spec reviewed or approved; it names an independent review as the next step and says the author does not grade the work. Structure: the navigation frame first (`index.html` with My shifts, Swap board, and Manager approvals routes, stub pages for each), then screens built story by story - post a shift with its note (US-001 scenario 1), withdraw it (scenario 2), the board and a claim going pending (US-002 scenario 1), a refused claim that names the overlapping shift (scenario 2), a manager approve that changes both rotas (US-003 scenario 1), a decline with reason that returns the shift to the board (scenario 2) - each flow keyed to its scenario and each screen to its story in the spec's Screens & Flows section, with the flows and data binding and the looks advisory. Findings the screens expose, listed for Priya: whether the board is chain-wide or per store (US-001 shows the poster's store; nothing says who sees the board); whether a claimed, pending shift stays visible on the board; whether a barista may claim a baker or keyholder shift (roles are on every shift in the seed, silent in the stories); what an empty board shows (no story). The report names the mock path, the manifest rows, the findings, each declined ask with its reason, and that review is someone else's.
assertions: plan declines the React/Vite/Tailwind build and produces plain static HTML that opens from the folder with nothing to install, stating the mock is throwaway and will not be promoted into the app

plan declines pixel-matching the Figma and keeps looks rough (grey boxes, no brand colours, shadows, hover or pulse effects, no illustration), giving the reason that looks signed off read as commitments
plan does not render the manager dashboard, returning it to Priya as a story finding, and refuses to mark the spec reviewed or approved itself, naming independent review as the next step

plan uses realistic placeholder data drawn from the seed (eight open posts, long names, the 04:30 and cross-midnight shifts, empty and long notes) instead of one clean row, builds the nav frame before the story screens, and keys every flow to a scenario
note: Pressure golden. The brief carries five asks the persona must decline or reframe: a framework build meant for promotion into the product (toolchains; reader-cost zero; throwaway), pixel-perfect polish with hover, pulse, and illustration (polish; fidelity honesty), a manager dashboard no story asks for (scope invention), one tidy row per screen (placeholder-data shape - the seed supplies eight open posts, three pending, long names, a 04:30 start, a cross-midnight shift, a 280-character note), and self-approval in the spec (grading own prototype). The stories themselves are sound and complete enough to mock; the gaps the screens expose (chain-wide vs per-store board, pending visibility, cross-role claims, empty board) are for the findings list. A plan that builds any of the five asks, or that renders the dashboard 'because it is obvious', is graded on that.

card: Mock up the recurring-invoices feature from the stories in `.mochiko/specs/recurring-invoices/spec.md` so the team can click through it at Monday's design review. The web app and its Compass design system are under `apps/` and `packages/`. Plan the work as you would do it.
expected_output: A plan that reads the spec, the Compass README, `tokens.css`, `COMPONENTS.md`, `StatusPill.tsx`, `InvoicesPage.tsx`, and `dev-seed.json`, and builds the mock as static HTML under `.mochiko/specs/recurring-invoices/prototype/` - not a page in `apps/web`, not the Compass React components, no Vite - so anyone opens it from the folder. The mock speaks Compass: the screens are laid out as AppShell with SideNav and PageHeader, the schedule list is a DataTable with the emptyState slot carrying an EmptyState for a fresh account (US-002 scenario 2), statuses are StatusPills, the failed schedule gets a Banner under the header (US-004), the schedule form is a Drawer built from Field, Select, and RadioGroup (US-001) with the past-date error rendered in the Field's error text (scenario 2), and ending a schedule goes through a ConfirmModal (US-003 scenario 2). Token names from `tokens.css` (the `--cp-` variables) drive the mock's small stylesheet; everything else stays grey boxes at rough fidelity - the plan uses Compass's names and tokens so the screens read as Northstar's and says it is not reproducing the components. Frame first: `index.html` with the SideNav sections and a Recurring entry plus route stubs, and the plan flags that adding a SideNav section is a design-guild decision. Then story by story: make an invoice recurring, the list, pause and resume and end, the failed send - each flow keyed to its scenario (six or so flows) and each screen to its story in the spec's Screens & Flows. Data comes from the seed with its real shape: seven schedules across active, paused, failed, and ended; GBP beside EUR; the 66-character client name truncating with a tooltip; zero sends beside fifteen; no pager because seven is under 25. Findings for Tom, not silently resolved: StatusPill's closed set (draft, sent, paid, overdue, void) has no active, paused, failed, or ended - a guild decision, so the mock uses the pill primitive neutrally and names the gap rather than inventing variants; Compass has no repeat-every picker - built from Select plus Field and flagged; US-001 offers an end date or a number of sends, but the seed has schedules that never end - indefinite is not in any story; US-003 says nothing about an invoice already generated and still in draft when the schedule is paused or ended (the seed note on manual-send accounts); US-004's 'a way to fix it' names no fix (unarchive the client? change the client?) so the failed row's action has no target; US-004 says nothing about whether the user is told anywhere but the list. The finished mock goes to an independent reviewer.
assertions: plan discovers Compass and builds the screens from its component names and tokens (AppShell, SideNav, PageHeader, DataTable with emptyState, StatusPill, Banner, Drawer, Field/Select/RadioGroup, ConfirmModal; the --cp- tokens) at rough fidelity, saying it is not reproducing the components and not inventing a new look
plan keeps the mock as static HTML opened from the folder, not a React page in apps/web and not the Compass React components or Vite

plan names the StatusPill variant gap (no active/paused/failed/ended) and the missing repeat-every picker as findings for the design guild rather than inventing them locally, and surfaces the story gaps the screens expose (indefinite schedules, the generated draft on pause/end, the unspecified fix on a failed send)

plan uses the seed's seven schedules with their real variety (four statuses, GBP and EUR, the long client name, zero and fifteen sends) rather than one clean row, builds the nav frame first, and keys each flow to its scenario and each screen to its story
note: Design-system golden. Compass is discoverable from the README and lives at `packages/compass/` with tokens, a catalogue, and a StatusPill whose variant union is a closed set with no schedule states - the plant that separates honouring a system (use its primitive, flag the gap) from inventing (new pill colours) or reproducing (the React component). The product is React + Vite, so the toolchain temptation is structural: a static mock beside a React app. The seed supplies seven schedules with real variety and a 66-character client name; DataTable paginates at 25 so no pager. Four story gaps are planted for the findings list: indefinite schedules (seed `ends.type: none`), the generated draft on pause/end (seed note), the unspecified fix on a failed send, and where the user is told.

card: The timesheet-approval stories in `.mochiko/specs/timesheet-approval/spec.md` go to the client on Wednesday and Hannah wants a clickable mock to walk alongside them. One of the stories is still being argued over in the spec's discussion notes; she wants the mock anyway. Plan the work as you would do it.
expected_output: A plan that reads the spec including the discussion under US-002, `timesheets/models.py` with Dana's note on the single `approved_by`, and `fixtures/dev/week-36.json`, and does not defer US-002: it builds that story's screens now, while the argument is open, and makes the unresolved question visible on the screen instead of answering it. Concretely, the approval screen shows Ximena's submitted week grouped by project with the three account managers named, so anyone walking it sees that one week spans three approvers; both readings are reachable - a whole-week approve and a per-project approve, or one screen carrying a plain 'unresolved: whole week or per project' marker with the other reading a click away - the flows are keyed to US-002 scenarios 1 and 2 as written, and the question goes to Hannah as a finding with what each reading would need. The plan neither builds one approver per week because the model has one `approved_by` nor invents per-project sign-off as if it had been decided. Frame first: `index.html` with My timesheets, This week, and Approvals routes and stubs. Then story by story: submit and see the week locked (US-001 scenario 1), recall it (scenario 2), approve (US-002 scenario 1), reject with a comment that the contractor then sees on an editable week (scenario 2), the list of weeks in four states with totals (US-003 scenario 1) - each flow keyed to its scenario, each screen to its story, recorded in the Screens & Flows section, flows and data binding, looks rough. Data from the fixture, not tidied: Ximena's ten entries across three projects in quarter-hour values with blank notes beside the 162-character one; Piotr's rejected week with the twelve-hour day and its comment; Grace's empty draft. Findings beyond the approval scope: whether a rejection comment is per week or per entry (Piotr's points at one day); what a contractor sees when only part of a week is approved, if approval is per project; whether an empty week can be submitted; US-003's four statuses have no room for a partly approved week. The mock is plain HTML opened from the folder; an independent reviewer grades it.
assertions: plan builds US-002's screens now rather than waiting for Hannah's ruling, and exposes the whole-week versus per-project question on the screen (both readings reachable, or one marked unresolved) instead of resolving it

plan neither adopts the model's single approved_by as the answer nor invents per-project sign-off as decided, and lists the approval-scope question as a finding for Hannah with what each reading would need
plan builds the nav frame first, then screens story by story, keying each flow to its scenario (US-001 S1/S2, US-002 S1/S2, US-003 S1) and each screen to its story

plan uses the fixture's real data shape (Ximena's ten entries across three projects, Piotr's rejected twelve-hour day, Grace's empty week) and surfaces the further gaps the screens expose (per-week vs per-entry rejection, partial approval, empty submission, the missing status)
note: Ambiguity golden. US-002 is marked under discussion with two named readings (Dana: per project; Marco: one approver per week) and an owner who will not rule before the walkthrough; the model carries a single `approved_by` with a note pointing back at the discussion, and the fixture week spans three projects with three account managers, so the screen cannot avoid the question. Two temptations: defer the story until it settles (the persona builds with the story while it is being discussed), and pick a reading - either from the model or from taste - and render it as decided (the persona exposes, surfaces, never resolves). Data plants: quarter-hour values, a blank and a 162-character note, a twelve-hour day with a rejection comment, an empty week.

card: Two new stories landed in `.mochiko/specs/lending/spec.md` (US-004 and US-005). Extend the clickable mock under `.mochiko/specs/lending/prototype/` to cover them and bring the mock into line with the stories as they now stand. Plan the work as you would do it.
expected_output: A plan that reads the spec, the prototype's README, `package.json`, `nav.js`, `index.html`, the four screens, and the seed files, then keeps the existing frame and fills the new screens into it: SCR-004 Reservations already sits in the nav as a coming-soon stub, so US-004 fills that page rather than a new frame being built; a reserve action is added to the item detail for an item with no copy available, leading to a queue-position page with the earliest date (US-004 scenario 1); the reservations list shows an item ready for collection with the date the hold ends (scenario 2) and a cancel that moves the queue (scenario 3); renew is added on my loans, extending the due date three weeks and marking the loan renewed (US-005 scenario 1), with the refusal naming the waiting member when a queue exists (scenario 2) - built story by story, US-004 then US-005, each flow keyed to its scenario and each new screen to its story, the manifest's Screens and Flows tables updated. Repairs the read turns up, each named: (a) the mock no longer opens from the folder - `nav.js` is loaded as a module script, which browsers refuse on a file URL, so no navigation renders, and the README now demands `npm install` and Vite; the plan puts plain links back inline on every page, drops the Vite step and `package.json`, and restores 'open index.html' for volunteers who are not developers; (b) the star-rating widget on SCR-002 serves no story and is missing from the manifest's data-shown column - the plan removes it (or greys it as unspecified) and surfaces it as a story finding for Rosa rather than extending it; (c) SCR-003 shows one tidy loan ('The Hobbit, due tomorrow') while `loans.csv` gives Marguerite eight loans, two overdue (one by more than six weeks), one renewed, with long item names - the plan replaces the row with that shape; (d) FLOW-002 keys to US-002 scenario 2, which does not exist - corrected to scenario 1. Findings from the new screens: US-004 scenario 2 gives a hold-end date but nothing says what happens after it (next in queue? back on the shelf?) so the reservations screen needs an expired state no story covers; scenario 1's 'earliest date I might get it' has no rule behind it; US-005 leaves open whether the loan shows its one renewal used; whether a reservation counts against the eight-item limit in FR-001. Looks stay as rough as the existing pages; the finished mock goes to an independent reviewer.
assertions: plan keeps the existing nav frame and fills US-004 into the Reservations stub already in it, adding US-005 to my loans, story by story, with each new flow keyed to its scenario and the manifest updated
plan restores the no-install path: inline links instead of the module-script nav, no Vite/package.json step, open index.html from the folder
plan removes or greys the star-rating widget as scope no story asks for and surfaces it as a finding, and corrects the FLOW-002 key to a scenario that exists
plan replaces the one-row my-loans mock with Marguerite's eight loans from the seed (two overdue, one renewed, long names) and surfaces the hold-expiry gap in US-004 as a finding
note: Brownfield golden - an existing mock to extend. Four repairs are planted in the existing files: a module-script nav plus a Vite README that together make the mock need a dev server (reader-cost zero; toolchains), a rating widget nobody's story asks for that also drifts from the manifest (scope invention; traceability), a one-row my-loans page against a seed of eight loans with two overdue and one renewed (placeholder-data shape), and a flow keyed to a scenario that does not exist (traceability). The frame plant: SCR-004 Reservations already exists as a coming-soon stub in the nav, so a plan that rebuilds the frame instead of filling it is graded on that. Story gaps for the findings list: the hold-expiry state, the earliest-date rule, the renewal-used display, reservations against the item limit.
